title: Riven
summary: Your Apple Watch knows when you've truly hit muscle failure
content: Riven: Your Apple Watch knows when you've truly hit muscle failure | Product Hunt Launching today Riven Launching today Your Apple Watch knows when you've truly hit muscle failure 82 followers Your Apple Watch knows when you've truly hit muscle failure 82 followers Visit website Fitness • Wearables Riven turns your Apple Watch into a muscle failure tracker. It auto-detects your exercise, counts reps hands-free, and measures rep speed loss — the science-backed signal of true muscle fatigue — to tell you if you actually trained to failure or stopped reps short. Built for hypertrophy and strength training: no camera, no bar sensor, no extra hardware — just the watch you already own. Get a 0–100 failure score after every set, so every workout drives real muscle growth. Overview Reviews Alternatives Team More Free Launch tags: Health & Fitness • Wearables • Fitness Launch Team Show more Show more Launching Today # 20 Day Rank Upvote • 89 points Follow Riven Add to collection Share Analytics Company Info riven.fit Riven Info Launched in 2026 Forum p/riven-reach-muscle-failure Similar Products Hevy Track workouts and join a community of gym athletes 4.9 ( 65 reviews ) Community management Workout platforms Impakt: AI Coach & Super Health App Get paid while getting fit. 4.6 ( 21 reviews ) Workout platforms Fitness Zing AI Fitness Coach AI-powered solution for hyper-personalized fitness training. 4.1 ( 8 reviews ) Workout platforms Fitness Train Fitness Automatic exercise detection & rep counting using AI Flex AI: Your AI Personal Trainer Introducing AI form feedback and AI-powered training coach. 5.0 ( 2 reviews ) View more Subscribe Sign in Framer Launch websites with enterprise needs at startup speeds. Try Framer Promoted What do you think? … Login to comment Baraa Bilal Maker 📌 Hey Product Hunt 👋 Here's an uncomfortable truth about the gym: most people never actually train to failure. They stop on discomfort, boredom, or a rep number they picked in advance — usually a few reps before the muscle is actually done. And since pushing close to failure is what makes muscle grow, that gap is why so many people train for years and look the same. Until now the only way to measure this was lab equipment — expensive, impractical, and definitely not something you'd use at a commercial gym. So I built Riven on something millions of people already wear: the Apple Watch. You just train. Riven detects your exercise, counts your reps, and at the end of every set tells you the one thing no app has ever told you — did you actually reach failure, or did you leave reps in the tank? No camera. No extra sensors. No tapping mid-set. Just the watch you already own. If you lift, I'd genuinely love your feedback — and ask me anything in the comments, I'll be here all day!
